events.description: This week's Play Date is cancelled. We will see you all next week, September 29! Join us on Tuesdays for special family play dates with museum educators! events.name: Nature Journaling
events.description: Drop by the Enid A. Haupt Garden between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. and join Smithsonian Gardens for nature journaling! Nature journaling is an opportunity for visitors to slow down, reflect, and connect to the gardens. This program is designed to foster appreciation and connection to the natural world through observation, reflection, and creativity. Smithsonian Gardens will provide journals, prompts, and art materials to get you started. All ages are welcome! Find us on the East Terrace of the Haupt Garden, close to the Arts and Industries Building. Recommended metro station: L'Enfant Plaza (Blue, Silver, Orange, Green, and Yellow lines) or Smithsonian (Blue, Silver and Orange lines). And be sure to check out the new Growing Tomorrow exhibition and discover how gardens connect people and plants! Activities may be subject to cancellation or modification due to weather conditions. Please check the Smithsonian Gardens online calendar for the latest information: https://gardens.si.edu/plan-your-visit/events/ This program received support from Smithsonian’s Our Shared Future: 250, a Smithsonian-wide initiative commemorating the nation’s 250th. events.venue: African American History and Culture Museum
events.description: For Ages: 8 and Up What does home mean to you? Is it a place, a person, a favorite object, a family tradition, or a memory you carry with you? Drop in for a hands-on zine-making experience that invites you to explore what home and belonging mean to you. Using photographs, drawings, words, collage, and other creative materials, create a one-of-a-kind zine inspired by the people, places, objects, traditions, and memories you treasure. Bring up to 3 printed personal photos to incorporate into your artwork. All other materials are provided. Reflect on the stories that shape who you are, share ideas with others, and leave with a personal keepsake that captures what “home” means to you. No previous art or zine-making experience is needed.

events.description: Beech Tree Puppets features meaningful stories, artfully told with hand-crafted puppets and sets and the use of simple instruments and beautiful singing. Ingrid and Ole Hass infuse Beech Tree Puppets with their professional experience in the performing and visual arts. events.name: Educator Workshop: Youth Civic Voice through Stamp Design
events.description: How can tiny postage stamps shape national narratives and amplify civic expression? In this hands‑on session from the National Postal Museum, participants will explore how stamps serve as primary sources that reflect and influence democratic values, U.S. identity, and civic engagement. Centering objects from the museum collection, we’ll examine stamp history, elements of design, and how stamps can elevate youth civic engagement. Participants will then create a stamp‑inspired print using simple, classroom‑ready printmaking techniques. This session blends visual arts, history, and civic learning through close‑looking strategies and hands-on learning that support the expression of civic voice through stamp design. This session is in collaboration with WISIT Institute, DC Project Zero.

events.description: Joie Chen, an Emmy-winning anchor and correspondent formerly of CNN, Al Jazeera, and CBS News will join directors Kim Jong-woo, Kim Shin-wan, and Cho Chul-young for an onstage conversation after the screening. Watch the Trailer On the night of December 3, 2024, then-president Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law in Korea. He banned all political activities and public assemblies and sent troops to the National Assembly building to seize control. The Seoul Guardians plunges you into the political chaos of that night, with codirecting by three journalists who were there. Lawmakers rush to pass a bill ending martial law as ordinary citizens band together to hold off the soldiers sent to take the building. The winner of multiple film festival awards, this stirring documentary resonates with audiences around the world with its message that democracy is fragile and must be defended. Even though it is very dark (except for the bioluminescent animals), the deepest parts of the ocean are still full of life. Together we will learn about some of the unique animals that have adapted to live in the deep sea, make artwork inspired by the deep sea, and have the chance to see specimens that once lived at the bottom of the ocean! events.name: Sneak Peek | Saodat Ismailova and Marianne Kamp in Conversation
events.description: Saodat Ismailova’s films weave together archival materials and her own footage to explore Central Asia’s layered histories and landscapes, from the region’s ancient past and Islamic traditions through the Soviet era and into the present. In this online program, Ismailova considers these subjects in conversation with Dr. Marianne Kamp, whose landmark studies of Uzbek social transformation have explored the lives of women and youth amid Soviet-era modernization and unveiling. Together, their reflections invite us to consider how personal memory, oral history, and historical archives can illuminate the political, social, and environmental changes that have shaped Central Asia. Born in Uzbekistan in 1981, Saodat Ismailova is an Uzbek filmmaker and artist living and working between Paris and Tashkent. She graduated from the Tashkent State Art Institute and Le Fresnoy—National Studio of Contemporary Arts in France. In 2021, she initiated Davra, a research collective dedicated to developing the Central Asian art scene. Ismailova participated in both the 59th Venice Biennale and documenta fifteen in 2022. The same year, she received The Eye Art & Film Prize (Amsterdam). In 2025, she received Foundation Pernod Ricard’s Nouveau Programme Award, was named an Art Basel Golden Awardee, and received the Han Nefkens Award for a new commission together with the Reina Sofía Museum (Madrid), Walker Center (USA), and the Singapore Museum of Arts. Her works are included in the collections of Tate Modern, London; Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam; Centre Pompidou, Paris; TBA21; FRAC Corsica; the Victoria and Albert Museum, London; and the Almaty Museum of Arts, Kazakhstan; among others. Marianne Kamp is an associate professor in the Central Eurasian Studies Department at Indiana University. She is a social historian of modern Central Asia who uses oral history methods to explore transformations in everyday life during the Soviet period and since the independence of the “-stans” in 1991. Dr. Kamp is author of Collectivization Generation: Oral Histories of a Social Revolution in Uzbekistan (Cornell 2024), The New Woman in Uzbekistan: Islam, Modernity, and Unveiling under Communism (University of Washington Press 2006); of an edited translation, with Mariana Markova, Muslim Women of the Russian Empire: Vladimir and Maria Nalivkins’ Nineteenth-Century Fergana Valley Ethnography (Indiana University Press, 2016); and of numerous articles and chapters. This program is part of the online lunchtime series Sneak Peek , where staff members and outside scholars share personal perspectives and new research related to the collections of the National Museum of Asian Art. events.name: ONLINE | In Conversation: Emma Alcazar and Nikki Corbett, Moderated by Veruschka Zarate
events.description: Hear from the designers of the second two block patterns in the museum’s Quilt Along. Quilter and fiber artist Emma Alcazar (Chickasaw) and artist, cultural educator, sewing instructor Nikki Corbett (Yup'ik) will discuss the inspiration behind their block patterns. The conversation will be moderated by Veruschka Zarate , quilt artist, international educator, and founder of Pride & Joy Quilting. This event will take place online via Zoom. Register now! Emma’s block pattern design responded to the theme of 20th century to present day (1902–2026). Download Emma's pattern to learn more. Nikki’s block pattern design responded to the theme of Our Shared Future (2026 and beyond). Download Nikki's pattern to learn more. About our speakers: Emma Alcazar (Chickasaw) is a Virginia-based quilter and fiber artist. Raised in Oklahoma, she holds a BA in Anthropology and MEd in Educational Leadership. After 18 years teaching English, she began focusing on creating art full time in 2022. She works with traditional quilting techniques, often incorporating Chickasaw or English language, to create hand-sewn art for display and use. Her quilts have appeared in multiple juried shows, including the Mid-Atlantic Quilt Festival, the Great Wisconsin Quilt Show, the Houston International Quilt Festival, and the Modern Quilt Guild’s QuiltCon; as well as at Exhibit C Gallery in Oklahoma City. Nikki Corbett is an artist, cultural educator, sewing instructor, wife, mother, and grandmother from Southwest Alaska, with family roots in Nunapitchuk and Bethel. She is the founder of Sew Yup'ik, a cultural arts initiative dedicated to revitalizing traditional Yup'ik sewing practices and passing knowledge to future generations. Her work centers on qaspeq (a hooded overshirt with large front pocket) making, nasqurrun (a Yup'ik woman’s dance headdress) revitalization, and traditional design elements that reflect ancestral teachings while engaging contemporary audiences. Her approach blends practical skill building with storytelling and emphasizes that Indigenous knowledge systems are living, evolving, and deeply relevant. Veruschka Zarate , the artist and designer behind Pride & Joy Quilting , is an award-winning quilt artist, pattern designer, international educator, and judge. Her quilts have been exhibited in museums and have earned some of the quilting industry’s highest honors including Best in Show at QuiltCon 2025, First Place in Piecing at QuiltCon, and QuiltCon People’s Choice. A proud firstborn daughter of a beautifully layered heritage, Veruschka’s roots span Puerto Rican, Cuban, Mexican, Irish, and French ancestry, along with Indigenous Taíno and Yaqui heritage. This rich intersection of cultures, histories, traditions, and stories has profoundly shaped the way she sees the world and continues to influence the artist, storyteller, teacher, and maker she has become. events.name: NY | The Americas Film Festival New York: "Uiksaringitara (Wrong Husband)"
events.description: In 2000 BCE Igloolik, Nunavut, star-crossed teenage lovers Kaujak and Sapa are promised to each other since birth, but their bond is shattered when Kaujak’s father dies and her mother marries a man from a distant camp. The promise of a better future turns into a desperate struggle as Kaujak is besieged by aggressive suitors backed by a powerful, evil shaman. Despite the pressure, Kaujak holds fast to her heart, resisting all attempts to claim her and clinging to the hope that Sapa will return to make good on their childhood pledge. The festival is a project of the Division of Interdisciplinary Studies at the Center for Worker Education of City College of New York (The City University of New York - CUNY), in collaboration with the Cervantes Institute of NY and the Smithsonian's National Museum of the American Indian. events.name: Broad Stripes and Bright Stars
events.description: Meet Mary Pickersgill, seamstress of the enormous garrison flag that inspired the lyrics to America’s national anthem and later became known as the Star-Spangled Banner. events.name: Theodore Roosevelt's North Dakota: Badlands, Bison, and the Making of a Conservationist
events.description: Over the course of the more than three decades he lived or visited there, the Badlands of western North Dakota transformed Roosevelt into the kind of vigorous outdoorsman that he’d idealized as a youth—and that shaped his public image as president. Perhaps more importantly, this corner of the West turned him into a passionate conservationist dedicated to the preservation of its rugged landscapes and native wildlife. Experience those landscapes on a 6-day study tour led by naturalist Melanie Choukas-Bradley that brings you into the heart of Roosevelt’s Badlands and the national park that bears his name.
